Bootstrap Test-Set Prediction Results

Overview

Every model is fit once on the same session-level stratified train set (seed=0, test_size=0.2). The test set is then resampled with replacement \(B = 1{,}000\) times to form 95% CIs on the held-out metrics.

The results are split into two figures, each keeping its models on an apples-to-apples evaluation scope:

  • Figure A — all rounds (incl. \(t=0\), “no-mask”): models evaluated on every round including the opening action. These have no subject-level memory at \(t=0\): OLS with only \(g, \ell, \delta\) and the Transformer trained without round-1 masking.
  • Figure B — rounds \(t \ge 1\) only (“mask”): models evaluated on rounds with at least one prior joint action. Includes OLS with joint \(n\)-gram history (\(+\) last 1…5), the Transformer trained with round-1 labels masked, and IRL-SG (defaults & MLE) scored on the same t≥1 rounds.

IRL-SG does predict \(t=0\) internally (using \(\sigma(\alpha + \beta \Delta_{RD} + e_i)\)), but its \(t=0\) probabilities use an individual-specific experience term \(e_i\) that accumulates across supergames — neither the OLS meta-only nor the Transformer have access to this. To keep Fig B comparable we score IRL-SG only on its in-game Markov-1 transitions (\(t \ge 1\)).

IRL-SG, briefly

Six-parameter model. Initial round (\(t=0\)): \(P(\text{coop}) = \sigma(\alpha + \beta \Delta_{RD} + e_i)\), with \(e_i\) an individual experience term that updates from the prior supergame’s initial action and total payoff. In-game rounds (\(t \ge 1\)): three fixed Markov-1 transition probabilities on the previous joint action — \(p_{CC}, p_{CD\_DC}, p_{DD}\) — defining a “semi-grim” strategy.

Parameters are either taken from the paper (defaults) or fit via differential_evolution MLE on the training set.

Out-of-sample metrics on the held-out session split, comparing the two Figure A (“no-mask”) models that predict every round including \(t=0\): OLS (g, l, δ) and Transformer (no-mask). Points show mean accuracy / AUC per supergame length, weighted by rounds (larger buckets => larger markers). Red line is a LOESS smoother.

Pairwise differences: does more history help? (Figure B models)

For each bootstrap iteration we compute the difference in test accuracy between adjacent OLS \(n\)-gram specs. If the 95% CI excludes zero, the improvement is robust.

IRL-SG: defaults vs MLE (scoring scopes side by side)

We score the same IRL-SG parameters in two ways: on all rounds (incl. \(t=0\), where the \(\sigma(\alpha + \beta \Delta_{RD} + e_i)\) initial-round logit + subject experience term contribute) and on \(t \ge 1\) only (just the Markov-1 transitions). The gap tells you how much of IRL-SG’s aggregate performance is driven by its initial-round component.
